reader.requirement: At 85 the GLOBAL clause may be written only in a data description entry whose level-number is 01 (spelled 01 or 1); the compiler must refuse GLOBAL on any 02-49 entry (in the File or Working-Storage Section), on a 77 entry, and on 66 and 88 entries, and must make a level-01 GLOBAL item and its subordinates visible to a contained program.

edition-consulted.switches: GLOBAL in the Linkage Section refused below 2002 (COBOL0900, construct linkage-global-2002); a section rule, not the level rule

reader.edition-search: The level-01 test (ClausePlacementRule.ResidenceFault: level != 1) consults no edition: ScreenClausePlacement and the Rules table carry no Edition/CobolVersion/ConstructRegistry reference (grep of DataBinder.ClausePlacement.cs). The only edition switch on GLOBAL is the Linkage Section gate in VersionConformancePass.VisitGlobalClause.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the level-01 restriction is the same code at every edition; at 85 the Linkage Section placement is additionally refused (a sibling rule).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f06_06 exercises the accept side (a level-01 GLOBAL group seen by a contained program); the refusal of GLOBAL at levels 02-49, 77, 66 and 88 is not exercised.

probes.expected: 01 GLOBAL, 1 GLOBAL (level-number spelled 1) with an ODO table and an FD 01 GLOBAL record are visible to the contained program, which can update them

probes.printed: error COBOL2404: data item 'G1-A': the GLOBAL clause is not admitted here — this entry's level-number is 05
error COBOL2404: ... this entry's level-number is 02
error COBOL2404: data item 'G1': the GLOBAL clause is not admitted here — this entry's level-number is 77
error COBOL1747: level-number 88 on 'G1-Y' ... this entry's body is not a value clause alone
error COBOL2404: data item 'F1-A': the GLOBAL clause is not admitted here — this entry's level-number is 05
probes.expected: refused: a subordinate of an FD record

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: the GLOBAL clause in the linkage section requires COBOL-2002

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.4.3.3 SR4  (4.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4

reader.notes: BindEntry calls ScreenClausePlacement, whose GLOBAL Residence row refuses any level other than 1 (77 included) and drops the clause, so a refused GLOBAL never registers a global name. The diagnostic cites the 2023 clause, which states the same level restriction. 66 and 88 never reach the row: the grammar/level screens refuse GLOBAL there.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: q3redef ('01 B REDEFINES A IS GLOBAL', GR3 form) -> compiles, contained program prints 'IN A BC' and its MOVE shows in the container 'OUT ZBC'; q3inner (GLOBAL on 03 inside a contained program's own 01 GLOBAL) -> COBOL2404 level 03; q3l02s (02 REDEFINES ... GLOBAL) -> COBOL2404 level 02; q3rptgrp (GLOBAL on a level-01 report group entry, whose 1985 format has no GLOBAL) -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'GLOBAL'; q3sd (01 GLOBAL record under an SD, File Section level 01) -> compiles, consistent with SR4 and §1985:X.4.6.3 SR1; q3const (a 2002 constant entry with GLOBAL) -> COBOL0900 requires COBOL-2002. The ScreenClausePlacement row consults no edition and the 1985 level-01 sentence is the same restriction. cite.py: OK  §1985:X.4.3.3 SR4  (4.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4.
